quiz.question: Under which Act was the 2022 Code of Good Practice on the Prevention and Elimination of Harassment in the Workplace issued?
options: The Occupational Health and Safety Act, 1993
The Banks Act, 1990
The Employment Equity Act, 1998
The Financial Sector Regulation Act, 2017
quiz.explanation: The Code was issued under the Employment Equity Act on 18 March 2022 (GN R.1890). The Banks Act and FSR Act govern prudential regulation, not workplace harassment.

quiz.question: A customer repeatedly makes sexual comments to a teller at the counter. Does the Code expect the bank to act?
options: No, the Code covers only conduct between employees
Yes, employers should try to protect staff from harassment by clients
Only if the customer holds an account at that branch and has been warned before
Only once the teller lays a criminal charge
quiz.explanation: The Code lists clients and customers among possible perpetrators and expects employers to attempt to protect employees from third-party harassment.

quiz.question: A manager sends one sexually explicit image to a junior colleague by text after work hours. Can this be sexual harassment under the Code?
options: No, because it happened after hours
No, because harassment requires a repeated pattern of conduct over several months
Only if the image was sent from a bank device
Yes, one incident can be enough and work-related messages are covered
quiz.explanation: The Code says a single incident of unwelcome sexual conduct may constitute sexual harassment, and protection extends to work-related communications through technology.

quiz.question: A supervisor hints that a staff member's training place depends on accepting his sexual advances. Which form of harassment is this?
options: Mobbing
Quid pro quo harassment
Horizontal harassment
Passive-aggressive harassment
quiz.explanation: Quid pro quo harassment is using influence over engagement, promotion, training, discipline or benefits to coerce someone into sexual advances. Mobbing is group harassment.

quiz.question: A complainant chooses the informal route. HR knows the alleged harasser has a history of similar complaints. What does the Code expect?
options: Assess the risk to others and, if significant, follow a formal procedure
Follow the informal route only, because the complainant's choice of procedure is always final
Transfer the complainant to protect her from further contact
Wait for a second complaint before doing anything
quiz.explanation: Item 10.8.2 says the employer should assess the risk to others, considering severity and history, and must follow a formal procedure if there is a significant risk, advising the complainant.

quiz.question: According to the Code, what can happen to an employer that does not take adequate steps after a harassment complaint is made within a reasonable time?
options: Nothing, because only the harasser is ever liable
The PA can withdraw its banking licence automatically
It can be held liable for the employee's conduct under section 60 of the EEA
The complainant loses the right to go to the CCMA
quiz.explanation: Item 10.3 explains that failure to take adequate steps renders the employer liable for the conduct under section 60, even for a single incident. It does not trigger automatic licence action.

quiz.question: Which statement best describes the training expectation in the Harassment Code?
options: Every employee must pass an annual government test
Only managers need training, by statute
Training is required only after a complaint is upheld against a manager at the workplace
Employers should include harassment in orientation and training, as good practice
quiz.explanation: Item 13 uses advisory language: employers should include sexual and other harassment in orientation, education and training. It is an expected competence, not a statutory exam or manager-only rule.

quiz.question: As summarised in the 2022 Code, what did the Constitutional Court reiterate in McGregor (2021)?
options: A harasser's seniority and a large age gap are aggravating factors
Senior employees cannot be dismissed for a first offence
Complaints must be made within 24 hours to be valid
Harassment by doctors is a matter for their professional councils, not employers
quiz.explanation: The Code's footnote records that in McGregor the Court reiterated that seniority and age disparity aggravate sexual harassment. It did not create the other rules.

quiz.question: Before the PA's governance review, the company secretary finds no training record for two new directors. What is the best readiness step?
options: Create training records from memory so the file looks complete before the PA's review starts
Record the gap, schedule induction training with an owner and date, and tell the board
Leave it out of the board report to avoid alarming the PA
Ask the directors to resign and be reappointed
quiz.explanation: Directive 1 of 2026 requires ongoing director training; readiness means honest evidence and tracked remediation. Invented records or concealment create a far worse governance problem.

references.title: Directive 1 of 2026 (D1/2026): Governance tenure
references.note: Replaces Directive 4 of 2018. The board-approved governance policy must ensure appropriate and ongoing training for directors, ongoing assessment of individual directors, and robust criteria so that only fit and proper people with the needed knowledge and skills are appointed.

references.title: Directive 1 of 2026 (D1/2026): Governance tenure
references.note: Independent chair and sub-committee chairs, cooling-off periods, minimum tests deeming a director not independent (including nine-year tenure with PA extension of up to 24 months), independence declarations, limits on other boards, BA 020 timing, PA supervisory review and exclusion of foreign branches.

references.title: Annexure A to Directive 1 of 2026: Banks Act, 1990 and Regulations (extracts)
references.note: Summarises the statutory duties: directors and executive officers owe a fiduciary duty and a duty of care and skill (s 60); the board must keep an effective corporate governance process (s 60B); the directors' affairs committee must regularly review the board's skills mix (s 64B).

references.title: Directive 7 of 2022 (D7/2022): matters related to fit and proper assessment of directors and executive officers
references.note: Banks are responsible for appointing fit and proper directors and executives and must assess them before and after appointment; BA 020 submissions need criminal background check reports (30 days for South Africans, 60 for foreign nationals), with disqualification for refusal and periodic re-screening.

references.title: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
references.note: The employer's general duty includes giving employees the information, instructions, training and supervision needed, as far as reasonably practicable, for their health and safety at work.

references.title: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993
references.note: Duty to inform employees of hazards; employees' duties including reporting; the CEO's responsibility; designation of health and safety representatives (more than 20 employees, at least one per 100 in shops and offices); committees meeting at least every three months; reporting of incidents. Text as published in 1993.

references.title: Code of Good Practice on the Prevention and Elimination of Harassment in the Workplace (GN R.1890, Government Gazette 46056)
references.note: Issued under the Employment Equity Act. Employers should adopt harassment policies and procedures, and should include sexual and other harassment in their orientation, education and training programmes in an accessible format.

references.title: Code of Good Practice on the Prevention and Elimination of Harassment in the Workplace (GN R.1890, Government Gazette 46056)
references.note: Scope (work-related settings, third parties), elements of harassment and the four-factor test for sexual harassment, guiding principles, informal and formal procedures, employer liability under EEA s 60 and confidentiality.

references.title: Media statement on VBS Mutual Bank, 11 March 2018 (curatorship)
references.note: Real case: the Governor tied VBS's liquidity crisis to the board's and management's failure to manage growth and funding; the bank was placed under curatorship and the board's powers passed to the curator.

references.title: VBS Mutual Bank investigators report to the Prudential Authority (The Great Bank Heist)
references.note: Real case: forensic report under FSR Act s 134, received 5 October 2018; finds almost R2 billion taken and that three non-executive directors admitted improper rewards.

references.title: South African Reserve Bank imposes administrative sanctions on VBS Mutual Bank (4 August 2017)
references.note: Real case: R2.5 million penalty (R2 million suspended) and remedial directives for weak FIC Act controls, months before curatorship.

references.title: Employment and Labour urges employers to comply with labour laws as non-compliance increases drastically in workplace (13 March 2024)
references.note: Real case: a Rustenburg blitz inspection testing OHS Act and other labour-law compliance issued contravention, prohibition and improvement notices and compliance orders.

bank.question: Sable Crest's controlling company has a board of 10. Seven are employees of the group. Which Banks Act rule is breached?
options: The rule that the board chair must also chair the controlling company's audit committee
The rule that every director must hold a banking qualification
The rule that at most 49% of its directors may be employees
The rule that boards may not exceed nine members
bank.explanation: Section 60 applies the 49% cap, rounded down, to controlling companies as well as banks: at most 4 of 10 directors may be employees. The other rules do not exist in the Act.

bank.question: Which of these is NOT one of the aims the Banks Act sets for a bank's corporate governance process under section 60B?
options: Guaranteeing a minimum dividend to shareholders each year
Avoiding or minimising conflicts between the bank's and directors' interests
Responsible conduct by directors and executive officers
Compliance with all applicable laws and regulations
bank.explanation: Section 60B lists conflict management, responsible conduct and legal compliance, alongside ethical and equitable achievement of objectives within acceptable risk. It does not guarantee dividends.

bank.question: An executive director of Sable Crest is asked to join the audit committee to 'add banking insight'. What does section 64 say?
options: Executive directors may join if they are not the CEO
One executive member is allowed if the chair agrees
Executives may join as non-voting members only by law
Audit committee members may not be employees of the bank or its group
bank.explanation: Section 64 requires all audit committee members to be non-employees of the bank, its subsidiaries, its controlling company and that company's subsidiaries. Executives can attend by invitation, but the Act gives them no seat.

bank.question: The remuneration committee has four members: three non-executive directors and the chief executive. What is wrong?
options: The CEO must chair the remuneration committee
Section 64C allows only non-executive directors on that committee
Remuneration committees need at least seven members, two of them employees
The committee must include the external auditor
bank.explanation: Section 64C, like section 64B for the directors' affairs committee, limits membership to non-executive directors. Having the CEO set or approve pay would create an obvious conflict.

bank.question: Under what power did the Prudential Authority issue Directive 1 of 2026 and Directive 7 of 2022?
options: Section 60B of the Banks Act
Section 6(6) of the Banks Act
Section 8 of the Occupational Health and Safety Act
Section 54 of the Employment Equity Act
bank.explanation: Both directives state that they were issued in terms of section 6(6) of the Banks Act. Section 60B is a governance duty, and the other sections belong to labour laws.

bank.question: When VBS Mutual Bank was placed under curatorship in March 2018, what happened to its board and management?
options: They kept running the bank under the curator's advice
They were replaced by PA staff on the board
They were required to recapitalise the bank within 30 days
They were relieved of their powers, which vested in the curator
bank.explanation: The Governor's statement explained that with a curator appointed, the board and management are relieved of their powers and these vest in the curator.

bank.question: Which element of the VBS story best illustrates a failure of the board's risk oversight, as described by the SARB in March 2018?
options: Taking large short-term municipal deposits and lending them out long-term
Opening too few branches in Limpopo
Refusing to pay out guaranteed retail deposits of up to R50,000 per depositor
Choosing Nedbank as the paying agent
bank.explanation: The Governor called it highly risky to take sizeable short-term municipal deposits and lend them long-term; this concentration and maturity mismatch drove the liquidity crisis. The Nedbank arrangement came later, under curatorship.

bank.question: A board pack contains a proposal in which a director's family company will supply the bank. The director stays in the room and votes. Which Banks Act aim is most directly at risk?
options: Keeping the audit committee free of employees
Keeping employee directors at 49% or fewer
Avoiding or minimising conflicts between the bank's and directors' interests
Having a risk and capital management committee with at least three board members
bank.explanation: Section 60B expects the governance process to minimise or avoid conflicts of interest, and Directive 1 of 2026 asks the policy to prevent them. Declaring and recusing is the normal control.

bank.question: A new non-executive director asks why the Banks Act governance duties matter to her personally rather than to 'the board'. What is the best answer?
options: Only the chair is accountable; other directors are advisers
Personal duties apply only to executive directors
Directors are personally liable only after curatorship
Section 60 makes each director owe the bank a fiduciary duty and a duty of care and skill
bank.explanation: The section 60 duties are owed by each director, CEO and executive officer individually. Non-executive status does not reduce them.

bank.question: Sable Crest's chair has just become a substantial shareholder through an inheritance. What should the board policy provide for under Directive 1 of 2026?
options: Automatic dissolution of the board until a new chair is elected
A fallback, such as a lead independent director, for a non-independent chair
Nothing, as the Directive only tests independence at appointment
Permission for the chair to continue as an independent for the rest of the nine-year tenure
bank.explanation: Paragraph 7.1.1.1 requires the policy to provide for a chair who becomes non-independent or conflicted, for example through a lead independent director. Continued non-independent chairing needs PA approval in exceptional cases.

bank.question: Under Directive 1 of 2026, which people must be independent non-executive directors, subject to narrow PA exceptions?
options: Every member of every board committee
The CEO, the chief financial officer and every member of the audit committee
The board chair and the chairs of the required board sub-committees
Only the chair of the audit committee
bank.explanation: Paragraphs 7.1.1.1 and 7.1.1.2 require an independent non-executive board chair and independent chairs of the required sub-committees. The PA may allow exceptions only in writing and in exceptional cases.

bank.question: A candidate was the bank's curator until 18 months ago. The board wants to appoint him as an independent non-executive director. What does the Directive say?
options: He may join as a non-executive, but not as independent within three years
He may be appointed as independent immediately
He may never serve on the bank's board
He may serve as independent at once if the PA confirms his BA 020 and his CV in writing
bank.explanation: A former curator faces a 12-month cooling-off before appointment as a non-executive, and having been curator in the preceding three years means he is not independent. Both tests apply.

bank.question: A director's spouse was a principal of a consultancy that was a material adviser to Sable Crest until two years ago, so an informed observer would doubt the director's objectivity. How should the board classify the director?
options: Independent, because the director never worked at the consultancy
Independent, provided the director declares the link annually
Not independent for life, regardless of time passed
Not independent, because an immediate family member falls within a disqualifying category
bank.explanation: The Directive deems a director not independent if an immediate family member falls within the listed categories, including a principal of a material adviser in the last three years where an informed third party would see a conflict. A declaration does not cure it, and the test is time-limited.

bank.question: A director who served as an independent director of a Sable Crest subsidiary for seven years is appointed to the bank's own board. What happens to his tenure?
options: He keeps counting from seven years, so he has only two years of independence left
He may never be independent at the bank level
He may reset the tenure, if the PA finds no material conflicts
He must first sit out a three-year cooling-off period
bank.explanation: Paragraph 7.1.2.8(b)(ii) allows a reset when a subsidiary's independent director moves to the bank or controlling company board, because the role is broader, provided the PA finds no material conflicts.

bank.question: Which statement about the nine-year rule in Directive 1 of 2026 is correct?
options: Beyond nine years a director is non-executive but not independent, unless the PA extends
The director must leave the board on the ninth anniversary
The rule applies only to the chair of the board
The board may extend independence by up to five years by special resolution, without the PA
bank.explanation: After nine years an independent director may remain as a non-executive director but not as independent. Only the PA may extend independence, in exceptional cases, in writing, for at most 24 months.

bank.question: A director completed nine years as independent, left the board, and is offered a seat again 20 months later as an independent director. What does the Directive say?
options: She is independent again after a 12-month break
She is not independent: she returns within three years after serving the tenure
She regains independence if the PA receives a new BA 020
She is independent again if she now holds fewer than 5% of the shares with her associates
bank.explanation: Paragraph 7.1.2.11 deems a director not independent if reappointed within less than three years after serving the nine-year tenure. Twenty months is too soon.

bank.question: Which supervisory process does the PA use to check that a bank's board-approved governance policy is complied with in practice?
options: An annual public hearing in Parliament
A certificate signed by the Companies Commission
A self-declaration lodged with the FSCA
Its supervisory review and evaluation processes
bank.explanation: Paragraph 7.2 says the PA assesses governance policies, processes, practices and their implementation as part of its supervisory review and evaluation processes.

bank.question: The Directive's training duty in paragraph 7.1.3.6 is classified as a role-based mandatory requirement. Who is it aimed at?
options: Directors of banks and controlling companies
Every bank employee, annually
Branch staff who handle cash
External auditors of banks
bank.explanation: The Directive requires appropriate and ongoing training for directors. Staff training duties come from other laws, such as the OHS Act and the FIC Act, not from this paragraph.

bank.question: Who may the PA require to submit a BA 020 even though they already hold office?
options: Only directors who change their address
Only directors who were appointed before 1990
No one, because BA 020 applies only to new appointments
Any serving director or executive officer, at the PA's request
bank.explanation: Directive 1 of 2026 records that regulation 42 requires a BA 020 for serving directors or executive officers when the PA requests it under section 1(1A)(c) of the Banks Act.

bank.question: A foreign national is proposed as Sable Crest's chief risk officer. His criminal background check report is 50 days old when the BA 020 is filed. Is it acceptable?
options: No, all reports must be under 30 days old
Yes, for a foreign national the report may be up to 60 calendar days old
No, foreign nationals need a report under 14 days old
Yes, because reports for foreign nationals never expire once the PA has accepted one
bank.explanation: Directive 7 of 2022 allows up to 60 calendar days for foreign nationals and 30 for South Africans. Fifty days is within the foreign-national limit.

bank.question: Sable Crest opens a banking subsidiary in another African country and appoints its directors. Does the criminal background check requirement apply?
options: No, it applies only inside South Africa
Only if the subsidiary is listed on a stock exchange in its host country
Yes, it also covers appointments in cross-border banking operations
Only for directors who are South African citizens
bank.explanation: Paragraph 2.1.11 extends the requirement to appointments in cross-border subsidiaries and branches established under section 52 of the Banks Act.

bank.question: Which pairing correctly links the regulatory document to its role in fit and proper assessments?
options: D7/2022 adds background checks; D1/2026 needs robust fit and proper criteria
Directive 7 of 2022 sets the director tenure limits; Directive 1 of 2026 sets the background checks
Both documents only cover executive officers
Directive 1 of 2026 abolished form BA 020
bank.explanation: Directive 7 of 2022 deals with background check reports supporting the BA 020, while Directive 1 of 2026 requires the policy to have robust criteria so only fit and proper people are appointed.

bank.question: Which quality is the PA expressly told to consider under section 1(1A) when looking at a director who sits on six other boards?
options: The person's home province
The diligence with which the person is likely to fulfil the responsibilities
The number of shares the person holds
The person's political affiliation
bank.explanation: Diligence is one of the three statutory qualities. Heavy board commitments can reduce the time and attention a director brings, which is why Directive 1 also requires limits on other boards.

bank.question: Why does Directive 7 of 2022 require banks to re-screen serving directors periodically rather than only at appointment?
options: Because BA 020 forms expire after 12 months
To replace the annual independence declaration
Because the PA no longer reviews appointments
To keep the bank's information about their criminal status up to date and accurate
bank.explanation: Paragraph 2.1.13 says re-screening keeps the information held up to date and accurate, supporting the bank's ongoing responsibility to keep fit and proper people in office.

bank.question: Which part of a sound director induction for Sable Crest best supports the 'competence and soundness of judgement' quality?
options: A tour of the head office building and parking
A list of board meeting dates for the year
Briefings on the bank's business model, risk profile and key regulatory duties
A gift pack and the director's email login
bank.explanation: Competence and judgement relate to the responsibilities of the office and the bank's risks. Induction on the business, risks and duties builds that; logistics do not.

bank.question: A group applies under section 12 of the Banks Act for authorisation to establish a new bank. What must the application include under Directive 7 of 2022?
options: Background check reports for every prospective director, executive and key person
Background checks only for the proposed chair and CEO
A sworn statement by the chair that no proposed director has a criminal record of any kind
Background checks only once the bank starts trading
bank.explanation: Paragraph 2.1.10 requires applications to establish a bank to include background check reports for every prospective director, executive officer and key person, before authorisation, not after.

bank.question: Which duty in section 8(2) of the OHS Act would require Sable Crest to ensure branch cash-handling work is overseen by someone who understands its hazards?
options: Section 8(2)(i): supervision by a person trained to understand the hazards
Section 8(2)(c): safety of articles and substances in transport
Section 8(2)(j): informing employees of the scope of their authority under section 37(1)(b)
Section 8(2)(b): eliminating hazards before using protective equipment
bank.explanation: Section 8(2)(i) requires general supervision by a person trained to understand the hazards and with authority to make sure precautions are implemented. The others address different aspects of the duty.

bank.question: Who must be informed beforehand when an inspector notifies Sable Crest of an inspection at its Durban office?
options: Every customer of the branch
The Prudential Authority
The health and safety representatives concerned
The bank's external auditors
bank.explanation: Section 13(b) requires the employer to inform the representatives concerned beforehand of inspections, investigations or formal inquiries an inspector has notified.

bank.question: Which employee is eligible to be designated as a health and safety representative under section 17(4)?
options: Any contractor who visits the workplace weekly
A full-time employee at that workplace who knows its conditions and activities
A part-time employee based at another province's office
An external consultant hired for the purpose
bank.explanation: Only employees employed full-time at the specific workplace and acquainted with its conditions and activities are eligible. Contractors and consultants cannot be designated.

bank.question: Sable Crest's East London branch has 18 employees. An inspector thinks a representative is still needed. What can the inspector do?
options: Nothing, because the duty to designate starts only once there are more than 20 employees
Appoint a representative from the inspector's own staff
Fine the branch manager on the spot
Direct the employer in writing to designate the number it decides
bank.explanation: Section 17(6) lets an inspector, by written notice, direct designation of representatives even where a workplace has 20 or fewer employees if the number is inadequate.

bank.question: During an armed robbery at a branch, a teller is injured and likely unable to work for at least 14 days. What does section 24 require?
options: Only the police must be told, because the OHS Act does not apply to criminal incidents
The teller must report it to the PA within 24 hours
The employer reports it to an inspector in the prescribed time and manner
Nothing, unless the teller later dies
bank.explanation: Section 24(1)(a) covers incidents at work causing injury likely to make a person unable to work for at least 14 days; the employer reports them to an inspector as prescribed. Robbery does not take it outside the Act.

bank.question: Which of the following is a function a health and safety representative MAY perform under section 18?
options: Investigate an employee's complaint about health or safety at work
Dismiss an employee who breaks a safety rule
Approve the bank's annual budget for facilities
Issue prohibition notices to the employer
bank.explanation: Section 18(1)(d) lets a representative investigate employees' safety complaints. Discipline and budgets belong to management, and prohibition notices are issued by inspectors.

bank.question: Sable Crest's board asks how it can show it meets section 8(2)(e). Which evidence is strongest?
options: A signed statement from the CEO that staff are safe
A copy of the Act on the intranet
Insurance cover for workplace injuries
Risk-based training plans, attendance records, supervision arrangements and drill results
bank.explanation: Section 8(2)(e) is about providing the information, instructions, training and supervision actually needed. Records of what was delivered and tested show that; a statement, a copy of the Act or insurance do not.

bank.question: A branch manager plans to rely only on giving staff anti-slip shoes after several falls on a wet entrance floor. Which OHS Act principle does this overlook?
options: Employees must pay for their own protective equipment unless a collective agreement says otherwise
Remove or reduce the hazard first, before relying on protective equipment
Only inspectors may decide on safety equipment
Protective equipment must be approved by the PA
bank.explanation: Section 8(2)(b) sets the order: remove or reduce the hazard first, for example mats, drainage and cleaning routines, before relying on protective equipment.

bank.question: Under the 2022 Code, whose perspective is the starting point when assessing whether conduct is harassment?
options: The intention of the alleged harasser alone
An objective assessment from the perspective of the employee who alleges harassment
The view of the majority of the team
The opinion of the line manager
bank.explanation: Item 4.4.5 says the assessment is objective, from the complainant's perspective, focusing on the impact of the conduct. The harasser's intention is not the test.

bank.question: A teller does not tell her supervisor his comments are unwelcome, but walks away each time he makes them. How does the Code treat this?
options: Silence means she accepted the comments
Only a written objection counts as showing it is unwanted
The conduct is harassment only if she reported it to HR within a day of each comment
Walking away or not responding can show the conduct is unwanted
bank.explanation: Item 5.2.1 recognises non-verbal ways of indicating conduct is unwanted, including walking away or not responding. And conduct can still be harassment where the perpetrator ought to have known it was unwanted.

bank.question: Which minimum statement should a harassment policy contain, according to item 9.4 of the Code?
options: Victimising an employee who lodges a good-faith grievance is a disciplinary offence
Complaints will be shared with all staff for transparency
Only sexual harassment will be investigated
Employees must first raise every complaint with the alleged harasser
bank.explanation: Item 9.4 lists statements including zero tolerance, confidential handling and that victimisation of a good-faith complainant is a disciplinary offence. Confronting the harasser is optional, not required.

bank.question: Where practicable, whom does the Code suggest employers designate for complainants to approach for confidential advice?
options: The alleged harasser's direct manager
The external auditor of the bank
A trained person outside line management, with suitable skills and resources
The chair of the board of directors
bank.explanation: Item 10.5.2 suggests a person outside line management, such as an employee, union representative or professional, who is properly trained and resourced.

bank.question: If internal procedures do not resolve a harassment dispute under the EEA, where may the complainant refer it, according to the Code?
options: Directly to the Prudential Authority
To the bank's audit committee, which gives a final and binding ruling on the dispute
To the Financial Sector Conduct Authority
To the CCMA or a bargaining council for conciliation, then adjudication
bank.explanation: Item 10.8.3.4 describes referral to the CCMA or a bargaining council for conciliation and then adjudication by the CCMA, bargaining council or Labour Court. The PA and FSCA do not decide harassment disputes.

bank.question: A disciplinary inquiry into alleged sexual harassment is being set up. Who should be present according to item 11.4 of the Code?
options: The whole branch team, so that the lessons from the case are shared with everyone at once
Any staff member who wishes to observe
Designated management, the parties, representatives, witnesses and any interpreter
Members of the media, for transparency
bank.explanation: Item 11.4 limits attendance to protect confidentiality. Opening the inquiry to the team or public would breach the confidentiality the Code expects.

bank.question: Which statement best describes how the harassment training expectation should be labelled in a South African bank's training map?
options: A mandatory annual course under the Banks Act
A competence expectation from a Code of Good Practice, not an express statutory training duty
A PA directive for all bank staff
An OHS Act requirement with a fixed frequency
bank.explanation: The Code uses advisory language for training and is guidance under the EEA. It should be delivered as good practice and to support the employer's section 60 position, but not labelled as an express statutory duty.

bank.question: Preparing for review, Sable Crest finds strong board training records but no record of harassment orientation for new branch staff. What should the readiness report say?
options: Name the gap, its risk, an owner and a date to add it to orientation
Leave it out because the PA reviews only board governance
Say all staff are trained, since the harassment policy has been on the intranet for a year
Postpone the report until the gap is closed
bank.explanation: Section 60B governance includes compliance with all laws, and honest gap reporting with owners and dates is what reviewers trust. Publishing a policy alone is not training.
